verdict: Robinhood's revenue rose 15% to $1.07B as event contracts quadrupled and interest income grew — and after heavier spending on growth and new products, profit was nearly flat at $346M.

segments.name: Transaction-based revenues
segments.note: Fees from trading: event contracts $147M (up 320%), options $260M (up 8%) and equities $82M (up 46%), partly offset by crypto $134M (down 47%).

segments.name: Net interest revenues
segments.note: Interest earned on customer cash, margin loans and securities lending — grew with interest-earning assets.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Robinhood Gold subscriptions ($50M, up 32%) and new services — the fastest-growing slice.

opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: Building and running the app and trading platform.

opex.name: Provision for credit losses
opex.note: Money set aside for cardholders and borrowers who may not repay.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and growth spending to win new funded accounts.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — up 31% with expansion and acquisition-related costs.

otherDetail: Other income (loss), net was $0M — a clean quarter with nothing material outside the main business.
footerNote: Robinhood does not report a separate cost of revenue; 'Brokerage and transaction' — the direct cost of executing customers' trades — is shown as the direct cost here. Net income of $346M is after a $4M loss attributable to non-controlling interests; $350M (EPS $0.38) is attributable to Robinhood.
follow100Note: Unlike last quarter there was no one-off gain in 'other income' — the $32.43 Robinhood kept of every $100 came from the business itself. Event contracts alone supplied $13.78 of every $100 of revenue.

takeaways.title: Event contracts quadrupled
takeaways.text: Event-contract revenue rose 320% to $147M and options rose 8% to $260M, more than covering a 47% drop in crypto revenue to $134M as digital-asset trading cooled.

takeaways.title: Customers kept depositing
takeaways.text: Net deposits were $17.7B in the quarter and total platform assets rose 39% to $307B; Gold subscribers grew 36% to 4.3M.

takeaways.title: Spending grew faster than revenue
takeaways.text: Operating expenses rose 18% to $656M — marketing, new products and acquisition costs — which is why profit rose only 3% despite 15% revenue growth.

oneTimers: Operating expenses included $14M of costs tied to launching Trump Accounts and the Rothera acquisition, flagged by Robinhood in its adjusted expense figures.
